week_label: Week of Sep 28 – Oct 2, 2026 · October in San Diego
note: Showroom feed — every image features real products SDLR installs, and each caption names the selections so followers can DM to get the look. Seasonal moment: no true holiday falls in this week, so Thursday Oct 1 is a tasteful 'first of October' post — San Diego's warmest, clearest month and the real start of outdoor-evening season. No autumn graphics, no promo, no urgency. Front-yard curb appeal returns Wednesday (Olivenhain lit entry court) — a week after the Point Loma driveway, holding the every-couple-weeks cadence. Shot mix rotates the five pillars across five distinct neighborhoods: La Jolla hilltop pool & fire (design/aspiration), a Mt. Helix mid-construction hardscape shot for craft & process — structure before landscaping (rare and high-trust), an Olivenhain geometric entry court at golden hour (neighborhood/curb appeal), an Eastlake pergola kitchen at dusk for the October post (lifestyle), and Rancho Santa Fe outdoor fireplace for trust & difference / Direct-Founder Access. All five images REUSED from the existing library — no new generation this run, no images pending. Post natively in the Instagram app.

posts.alt: La Jolla hilltop backyard at dusk with an infinity-edge pool, linear fire pit, teak lounge seating and a built-in outdoor kitchen against a canyon view
posts.hook: A view is only half of it. The other half is where you sit to watch it.
posts.caption:
Most hillside lots get treated like a lookout — a slab, a railing, and a view nobody actually stays out for.

The fix is furniture-first planning. The lounge sits low and forward so the fire reads against the water and the horizon lines up behind it. The pool edge disappears into the canyon. The kitchen tucks under the roofline so the cook never has their back to the sunset. Same view, entirely different evening.

The selections:
• infinity-edge pool with glass-tile waterline
• linear fire pit, Warming Trends CrossFire burner
• Lynx built-in grill with stainless cabinetry
• large-format porcelain pavers
• FX Luminaire low-voltage lighting

Want the view worth staying out for? DM “DESIGN”.

posts.alt: Mt. Helix hillside backyard mid-construction with poured concrete seat walls and planter walls, a rebar-reinforced fire pit form, stacked travertine pavers on pallets and a valley view
posts.hook: This is the week nobody photographs. It's the week that decides everything.
posts.caption:
Every finished backyard you've ever admired looked like this first.

Walls poured and cured before a single paver is set. The fire pit built as a reinforced structure, not a kit dropped on grade. Base compacted in lifts. Drainage sleeved and pitched while the ground is still open — because the one thing you can't add later is what's underneath.

A yard fails from the bottom up. So we spend the money where you'll never see it, and the finish stays flat, dry and tight ten years in.

The selections:
• engineered concrete seat & planter walls
• rebar-reinforced fire pit structure
• compacted Class II base in lifts
• sleeved subsurface drainage
• travertine pavers, staged for set

Want to see how yours would be built? DM “DESIGN”.

posts.alt: Olivenhain modern stone-clad home at golden hour with a geometric paver entry court in three finishes, recessed linear step and border lighting, and drought-tolerant planting
posts.hook: The entry court is the only room in the house every guest walks through.
posts.caption:
Front yards get the leftover budget and the default pour. Then the same homeowner wonders why the arrival feels flat.

This one is laid out like an interior floor: three finishes — honed limestone, exposed aggregate, and a darker banded stone — set in a geometry that pulls the eye straight to the door. Recessed linear lighting washes the surface at dusk instead of spotlighting it. Nothing here is decoration; the pattern is doing the wayfinding.

The selections:
• large-format honed limestone pavers
• exposed-aggregate contrast banding
• recessed linear step & border lighting
• stone-veneer façade surround
• agave, yucca and ornamental grasses

Want your arrival to match your home? DM “DESIGN”.

posts.alt: Eastlake backyard at dusk with a dark-stained pergola over a stone-faced outdoor kitchen and bar seating, a round fire pit with sectional lounge, paver patio, turf panel and agave in planters
posts.hook: October 1. The month San Diego quietly saves for itself.
posts.caption:
Everywhere else, today is the start of staying in. Here it's the opposite.

October is San Diego's clearest, warmest, stillest month — the marine layer's gone, the crowds are gone, and the evenings hold their temperature past ten. It's the stretch a backyard is genuinely built for, and it runs right through Thanksgiving if you have the fire.

This one is a standard suburban lot, used completely: pergola over the cooking and bar so there's shade at four and light at eight, fire pit and sectional squared off the patio, a turf panel to keep the whole thing usable in bare feet. No wasted corner.

The selections:
• stone-faced outdoor kitchen with bar seating
• cedar-stained pergola with café string lighting
• Belgard Urbana paver patio
• round gas fire pit, sectional lounge
• SYNLawn turf panel + agave in planters

Want the October evenings back? DM “DESIGN”.

posts.alt: Rancho Santa Fe backyard at sunset with a tall stacked-stone outdoor fireplace, curved built-in seating around a round fire feature, travertine paving, olive trees and lavender
posts.hook: Ask who will actually be standing in your yard on Tuesday morning.
posts.caption:
A curved seat wall is a good test of a firm. It has to be set out in the field, adjusted against the real grade, and finished by someone who has done a few hundred of them. Get it wrong and the radius fights the fireplace for the rest of the home's life.

Which is why Gio and Mike are in it directly — not an account manager relaying notes. You talk to the two people who own the outcome, and our lead craftsman, 25+ years in high-end outdoor work, is the one setting the line. Then we come back at ten months and walk the whole thing with you.

One firm. One plan. By design, not by dispatch. References available on request.

The selections:
• Eldorado Stone stacked-stone fireplace
• curved built-in seating with cushions
• round gas fire feature
• French-pattern travertine paving
• mature olives, lavender & ornamental grasses
